claims.text: Example repo @ stage-4: deploy/tofu/envs/production/cluster/main.tf describes only a lab cluster, the same kind-cluster module as staging (name donhang-production, one control plane, 2 workers), and OpenTofu only plans it; in the lab nothing runs production.
Kubernetes itself has no licence fee; it is open-source software.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Overview (open-source system); docs/team/self-run-components.md line 3

claims.text: Self-running with kubeadm: the team builds the control plane, keeps an etcd majority (quorum), upgrades and is on call. Bare metal lacks cloud parts; in ADR 0022 option A, MetalLB gives the Gateway an address and Longhorn copies volumes between nodes.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Operating etcd clusters (quorum); kubeadm HA topology; ADR 0022 option A lines 31-34; k8s.l3.clusters-without-a-cloud

claims.text: A managed Kubernetes service runs the control plane and its upgrades for a fee; node pools add nodes for peaks; the team still runs what runs on the nodes.

ADR 0022 @ stage-4: the multi-shop system (ADR 0012) must run continuously for every shop, absorb seasonal peaks and be run by one team; figures are assumptions over three years, not a provider's price; fees converted to team days.
ADR 0022 table (monthly, assumed): A own machines 6 team days + 3 fees = 9; B managed one provider 2 + 4 = 6; C two providers 5 + 7 = 12.

ADR 0022 decision: chooses B because one team cannot keep a control plane and replicated storage running around the clock and node pools grow for peaks while own machines are bought ahead; C rejected: doubles the platform for a risk the exit plan covers.
ADR 0022 option C: running on two providers at once doubles the platform to run and limits the system to what both providers offer.

ADR 0022 lines 49-50: the database and other self-run components stay as self-run-components.md says (PostgreSQL self-run: the team upgrades and backs it up); the ADR decides only where the cluster runs.

ADR 0022 lock-in points: StorageClass names in manifests with volumes; provider load balancer in front of the Gateway (instead of lab NodePort and MetalLB); key service (ADR 0023: the provider's HSM service holds the invoice signing key); OpenTofu code of the cluster layer.
ADR 0022: manifests, Kustomize overlays, Argo CD and the config repository, admission policies move unchanged; Secrets are sealed again with the new cluster's key; no managed-cluster code at stage-4.

ADR 0022 exit plan: build a new cluster beside the old from the config repo, fix the lock-in points, move data by base backup and WAL, switch traffic; rehearsed on staging. Reopen: contract needs own machines or data in a set place; provider's fee alone (B: 4) passes column A's cost (9).
ADR 0022 'Ý kiến đã nhận': the product owner asked about two providers for better pricing; answer: the exit plan gives that position without running two platforms; decision unchanged.
A PersistentVolumeClaim whose storageClassName names a StorageClass that does not exist in the cluster is not provisioned and stays Pending.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Persistent Volumes > Class; Dynamic Volume Provisioning

claims.text: Arithmetic from ADR 0022 table: A < 6 needs team days < 3 (fee 3); B > 9 needs fee > 7 (team days 2). The second condition compares the fee alone with A's 9, so read literally it fires later than 7. Opinion: team days count effort, not round-the-clock cover.

Opinion (trade-offs table): A puts control plane and peaks on the team with no provider ties; B trades a fee and four lock-in points for less team work; C removes the tie to one provider at the cost of two platforms and the common feature set.
claims.source_hint: trade-off reasoning; ADR 0022 options and consequences

claims.text: Opinion: when a contract requires own machines or data location, reopen ADR 0022 and compare with the contract as a driver; when the fee alone passes column A's cost, redo the table with measured figures; when asked for two providers for pricing, keep B.
claims.source_hint: ADR 0022 reopening conditions and received comments

claims.text: Opinion: multi-cloud as protection against lock-in shows up as releases tested on two platforms and provider features left unused; same reasoning as rejecting an abstraction for a switch nobody needs yet.
